record.original_question: Let L_d be an n^(1/d) by ... by n^(1/d) integer lattice in R^d. Determine the asymptotic order of subset(L_d), the largest size guaranteed for a subset in which no positive distance is repeated.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $d\ge 2$ and a positive integer $n$ such that $n^{1/d}$ is an integer, let
$$L_d = \{1,2,\ldots,n^{1/d}\}^d \subset \mathbb{R}^d$$
be the $n^{1/d}\times\cdots\times n^{1/d}$ integer lattice (so $|L_d|=n$). Define
$$\mathrm{subset}(L_d) = \max\{|S| : S\subseteq L_d \text{ and the Euclidean distances } \|p-q\|, \ p\neq q \in S, \text{ are pairwise distinct}\}.$$
Determine the asymptotic order of growth of $\mathrm{subset}(L_d)$ as $n\to\infty$ (with $d$ fixed). It is known that
$$\Omega\!\left(n^{2/(3d)}\right) \le \mathrm{subset}(L_d) \le O\!\left(n^{1/d}\right);$$
close this gap and find the true asymptotic value.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem, posed by Erdős and Guy, asks for the asymptotic size of the largest subset of an integer lattice in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with all pairwise distances distinct. The best known bounds remain $\Omega(n^{2/(3d)})$ (Lefmann–Thiele, 1995, with a logarithmic improvement for $d\ge 3$) and $O(n^{1/d})$. No further progress closing this gap has been reported in subsequent surveys, and the problem is still listed as open.

status_evidence.snippet: Lefmann and Thiele improved the bound to subset(L_d) = Ω(n^{2/(3d)}); the points of L_d span O(n^{2/d}) distinct distances, implying subset(L_d) = O(n^{1/d}).
status_evidence.claim: Bounds Ω(n^{2/(3d)}) ≤ subset(L_d) ≤ O(n^{1/d}) are the best known and the asymptotic value remains an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Point sets with distinct distances (Lefmann–Thiele)
status_evidence.claim: Lefmann and Thiele established the current best lower bounds, with no matching upper bound known.
